assessment.nobel_worthiness: A discovery in the sense I care most about: nature supplied the clue. IceCube established a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and opened neutrino astronomy, with the 2017 TXS 0506+056 coincidence and the later NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane evidence. It is original in instrumentation (a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice) and it addresses the origin of cosmic rays, a question open for a century.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely regarded as the intellectual driver of the IceCube concept and its science case; Spiering is credited with long-term leadership and the AMANDA-to-IceCube lineage. The list omits other names (for example, leadership of the collaboration or the DUMAND and AMANDA pioneers) that might be argued for, so two names is a defensible but not airtight configuration. I rely on my own recollection of the history rather than any independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by the independent ANTARES/KM3NeT-era detections only partially; the diffuse flux is solid and the source associations are now accumulating evidence at several sigma. Timing is good: the field has matured past the first-evidence stage but the source picture is still developing.
uncertainties: Whether the source-identification evidence (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) is regarded as decisive enough or whether the committee should wait for firmer source catalogues.
Allocation of credit between the founding figures and the present collaboration leadership is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty are a landmark of precision measurement. Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's realisation of record accuracy give a new window on fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and possible dark-sector tests. The lasting impact on metrology and the planned redefinition of the second is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye demonstrated the strontium clock at the highest accuracy and developed the underlying frequency-comb and laser-stabilisation methods. This is a clean two-person configuration, though Hall and Hansch were already recognised for combs and ion-clock groups (Wineland) are in a nearby area.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in several laboratories (strontium, ytterbium) with agreement at the 10^-18 level; the technology is mature. Recognition is timely, with the redefinition of the second under discussion.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes in frequency metrology (2005, 2012) may reduce the perceived novelty.
Whether ytterbium clock groups or other contributors deserve credit is not captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices turned strongly correlated many-body physics into a controllable laboratory system: the Mott insulator transition, Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site imaging with quantum gas microscopes. It is original, widely adopted and links condensed matter, AMO and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: The experimental line is clearest for Bloch (Mott insulator with Greiner and Hansch, lattice many-body programme), Greiner (quantum gas microscope, Mott insulator) and Esslinger (Fermi gases and Fermi-Hubbard in lattices). Zoller and Cirac made the theoretical proposals and could also be justified, but the cap of three forces a choice; the list also contains a separate theory entry. The Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 and the credit due to Jaksch-Zoller make the allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups over two decades. The field is mature, although the claim that the simulators solve problems classical computers cannot is still under development.
uncertainties: Whether the experiments or the theoretical proposals are regarded as the decisive step.
Possible overlap with the Bose-Einstein condensation and quantum-information prizes already awarded.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field, moire quantum materials. It is exactly the kind of theory-and-experiment pairing where a prediction is confirmed by nature. It has produced many follow-up discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero led the decisive experiments in 2018; Bistritzer and MacDonald gave the theory that identified the magic angle. MacDonald-Bistritzer is the natural theory credit, so this three-name set is coherent. Others (Cory Dean, Kim, Yacoby, Young, and the Santa Barbara and Columbia groups) are not on the list but contributed to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups; the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism and the correlated phases remains under study, so the field is still moving.
uncertainties: Whether the pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is sufficiently understood.
Credit for the experimental side beyond Jarillo-Herrero is not resolved by the supplied names.
Timing may be a few years early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler that has independently measured cosmic expansion and strengthened the evidence for dark energy. It is directly relevant to the greatest open problem in my field, and is a clean example where a theoretical feature (acoustic peak) was found in the data.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 SDSS detection (Eisenstein et al.) and the 2dFGRS detection (Cole, Percival et al.) were contemporaneous and independent. Peacock leads 2dFGRS but the decisive analyses carry the other names, so I pick three. Theory of the acoustic peak (Peebles-Yu, Sunyaev-Zel'dovich) predates these and raises a credit problem that the supplied names do not solve.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by SDSS, BOSS, eBOSS, 6dF, WiggleZ and now DESI; the interpretation is robust, but recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy are not settled.
uncertainties: Prior theoretical credit (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zel'dovich) is outside the supplied names.
Dark-energy interpretation is still evolving, which may make the prize looks like a partial recognition of an incomplete story.
Dark energy was already recognised in 2011.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging of M87* and Sgr A* gave direct visual evidence of the black-hole shadow, a long-anticipated strong-field test of general relativity. The importance for gravity and black-hole physics is high and the experimental feat (global VLBI at 1.3 mm) is remarkable.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT and the VLBI technique development, Moran led the earlier mm-VLBI and Sgr A* work. The result is a large collaboration of several hundred people, which complicates the three-person cap.
assessment.maturity: Results from 2019 and 2022 are recent; polarisation and multi-epoch data are consistent, but the precision of GR tests is modest. Black holes were recognised in 2017 and 2020, so some redundancy.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit does not map neatly to three individuals.
The tests of GR are not yet competitive with gravitational-wave constraints.
The black-hole theme was recently recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The kilonova and its link to r-process nucleosynthesis, with GW170817 and AT2017gfo, is a multi-messenger discovery that identified a major origin of the heaviest elements. It touches nuclear physics, gravity and astrophysics and also says something about where we come from.
assessment.attribution: Metzger (kilonova modelling), Kasen (radiative transfer and r-process opacities) and Tanvir (observation of the 2013 GRB 130603B kilonova candidate) give a theory-plus-observation configuration. Lattimer-Schramm (the original idea) and Li-Paczynski are outside or only partly covered by the supplied credit, and the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: GW170817 is a single well-observed event; later events have not provided a second clear kilonova, so independent confirmation is limited and r-process yields remain debated against collapsars.
uncertainties: Only one confirmed multi-messenger kilonova; relative contribution to r-process is debated.
Credit for the early prediction (Lattimer, Schramm, Li, Paczynski) is partly outside the list.
The Nobel for gravitational waves in 2017 may reduce the appetite.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Transmission spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres turned exoplanets from points into worlds with chemistry: sodium, water and later more complex molecules, with JWST now providing detailed spectra. It carries the existential dimension I mentioned when announcing the 2019 prize, and builds on that prize.
assessment.attribution: Seager made early theoretical predictions of atmospheric signatures, Charbonneau made the first detection of an atmosphere (sodium in HD 209458b), Tinetti is credited for the water detections and for the ARIEL mission. The decisive contributors are plausible but the roles overlap with other groups (Brown, Swain, Tinetti and Deming), so the attribution is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Early detections were occasionally contested, and JWST is now reshaping the field; the interpretation of individual spectra is still evolving, so this may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Disputed early detections and strong dependence on retrieval models.
Recognition in 2019 for exoplanets reduces the case for a rapid second prize.
Attribution among many groups is not clear.
